original_question: Can one solve d-bar with Hölder estimates on any real analytic bounded pseudoconvex domain in C^n ? 6.3
target_in_paper: Section 6, Problem 6.3: "Can one solve \bar\partial with Hölder estimates on any real analytic bounded pseudoconvex domain in \mathbb{C}^n?"
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the core content of the paper's target problem: it names the correct operator (\bar\partial), the sought regularity/estimate type (Hölder estimates), the geometric class of domains (bounded pseudoconvex with real analytic boundary), the ambient space (\mathbb{C}^n), and even the internal locator "6.3."
missing_details: The draft is not fully stand-alone: it should quantify over an arbitrary bounded pseudoconvex domain \Omega \subset \mathbb{C}^n with real analytic boundary.
It should make explicit that "solve \bar\partial" means solving \bar\partial u = f for \bar\partial-closed data f.

The bidegree/form degree of the data and solution is not specified; the terse problem-list entry leaves this implicit, but a stand-alone formulation should at least acknowledge that the question concerns the relevant \bar\partial-closed forms.
The phrase "with Hölder estimates" is not unpacked: a stand-alone version should indicate that one is asking for a global solution operator bounded in Hölder spaces up to the boundary.
The Hölder exponent(s) and exact norm inequality are not stated; these are not spelled out in the problem-list entry, but they are needed for a mathematically self-contained formulation.
It is not explicit whether the question is local or global; in this context it should be read as a global boundary-regularity question on the whole bounded domain.
The draft does not say whether the boundary regularity assumption is on the domain boundary; a stand-alone wording should say "with real analytic boundary."
refined_question: Does every bounded pseudoconvex domain \Omega \subset \mathbb{C}^n with real analytic boundary admit a global solution theory for the \bar\partial-equation with Hölder estimates; equivalently, for every such \Omega, can one solve \bar\partial u=f for \bar\partial-closed data f in the relevant bidegrees by a solution operator that is bounded in Hölder spaces up to the boundary?
justification: The draft is already very close to the official problem-list wording, and the paper's entry is itself terse. The refined version therefore stays narrow and does not broaden the question to smooth, finite-type, convex, or other neighboring classes of domains. It only makes explicit the universal quantifier over bounded pseudoconvex real-analytic domains in \mathbb{C}^n and the implicit meaning of solving \bar\partial "with Hölder estimates" as the existence of a global Hölder-bounded solution operator for \bar\partial-closed data. No alternate formulation is given because the paper does not, in the accessible problem-list entry, state an explicit equivalent reformulation for Problem 6.3.
